name: UMI
summary: UMI is a hand-held parallel gripper with a wrist camera, fisheye side mirrors for implicit stereo, and IMU-aided visual-inertial odometry, letting anyone record demonstrations in any environment. Careful interface design plus latency matching between recording and policy inference means hand-collected data transfers to a real arm, enabling dynamic (tossing), bimanual, precise and long-horizon skills with zero robot time during collection.
innovation: Decoupled data collection from robot hardware entirely: the demonstrator is the gripper.
Explicit latency matching between human recording and robot execution so dynamic skills transfer.
Side mirrors providing implicit stereo from one cheap camera.
matters: Opened a path to in-the-wild manipulation data at internet scale; widely copied and extended.
limits: Limited to one parallel-jaw morphology, with no force or torque sensing.
lineage: Data-collection hardware designed specifically to feed Diffusion Policy training.
